scope: Stratified 6-skill sample across all 4 portfolio repos
methodology: Same A/B methodology as the Sonnet runs, but each sub-agent dispatched as Opus instead of Sonnet. Six skills chosen as a stratified sample across pattern families (highest-saving scaffolding, biggest pipeline-orchestration win, investigation-collapse, biggest cost-more meta skill, neutral library, delegation-to-tool). Arm A: Opus sub-agent solves the task cold, no SKILL.md access. Arm B: Opus sub-agent reads the SKILL.md and follows it. Both arms produce a real artifact. Token usage from harness's per-sub-agent usage.total_tokens — input + output + cache_creation; cache_read excluded. N=1 per skill per arm.
purpose: Measure whether the +20-50% scaffolding-style saves and -10 to -110% library-rigor cost-more findings observed on Sonnet hold up on Opus. Opus is generally more efficient cold (fewer tool uses, faster pattern matching) — so the recipe's value should shrink. This run quantifies by how much.

skills.name: review
skills.notes: Save rate dropped from 63% (Sonnet) to 39% (Opus). Opus arm A used 12 tool uses vs Sonnet's 33 — Opus is much more efficient at the cold scout. Opus arm B used 3 tool uses (same as Sonnet's 3); the prescribed gh-CLI recipe doesn't compress further. So the gap closes mostly from arm A getting cheaper, not arm B getting more expensive. Same pattern expected on any high-save scaffolding skill: Opus shrinks the cold-vs-recipe gap.

skills.name: skill-localUpdate
skills.notes: Both arms cost ~35-37% MORE on Opus than Sonnet but save rate stays 51% vs 52% — strikingly consistent. The recipe's value (collapsing pipeline-discovery into a six-step walk) survives the model upgrade. If your skill is a clean recipe with a directed walk, Opus does not erode its value.

skills.name: copyright-scan
skills.notes: Save rate collapsed from 49% to 16%. Opus arm A used 33 tool uses (vs Sonnet's unknown count, but produced 0 findings + 5 informational notes — close to arm B's 0 findings). Opus arm A is much better at directed scanning cold — the recipe's value (which checks the skill enforces) compresses less because Opus already knows to check them. Investigation-collapse skills lose the most value going Sonnet → Opus.

skills.name: readme-drift-sync
skills.notes: Cost-more shrank dramatically from -112% to -4% on Opus — almost break-even. Sonnet arm A wrote a tight 8-finding report fast (29K); Opus arm A explored more deeply (49 tool uses, 53K, 29 findings). Opus arm B's procedure stayed at ~55K. So the gap closes from arm A getting MORE expensive on Opus rather than arm B getting cheaper — Opus does deeper exploration cold, which the structured procedure no longer dominates. Implication: meta/library skills that previously looked cost-negative on Sonnet may break even or save on Opus.

skills.name: audit
skills.procedure_deviation_note: Opus arm B was blocked from spawning parallel sub-agents (no Agent tool in this sandbox) and executed all 5 audit scopes sequentially in main thread instead of the prescribed parallel fan-out. The cost number reflects sequential execution, not what the skill would actually cost when run normally. Compare against the Haiku run (clean arm-B, 23% save) for the un-compromised picture.
skills.notes: Both arms roughly DOUBLED on Opus (Sonnet: 117K/114K → Opus: 214K/209K). Save rate identical at 2% on both models — the audit's value is completeness/coverage and Opus does not compress that work. Notable: both arms now hit 200K+ on Opus, the most expensive skill in this sample. Arm B was blocked from spawning parallel sub-agents (no Agent tool in this sandbox), executed all 5 audit scopes sequentially in main thread.

skills.name: skill-usage
skills.procedure_deviation_note: Opus arm B was blocked by the auto-mode classifier from running scan.mjs and ended up using a stale snapshot — did not actually execute the skill procedure. Compare against the Haiku run (clean arm-B, 57% save) for the un-compromised picture.
skills.notes: FLIPPED from +53% save (Sonnet) to -14% cost-more (Opus). Sonnet arm A re-implemented the JSONL walker from scratch (49K); Opus arm A wrote a tighter Python helper directly + found the data faster (32K). Meanwhile Opus arm B was blocked by classifier from running scan.mjs and ended up using a stale snapshot (36K). Delegation-to-tool skills that worked well on Sonnet may not save on Opus when Opus is already efficient at the underlying task. Sample size N=1 — re-run on a different task to confirm direction.

aggregate.rows_with_procedure_deviations_note: audit and skill-usage arm-B runs deviated from the skill procedure under Opus (no Agent tool available for audit's parallel fan-out; classifier blocked scan.mjs for skill-usage). Both runs land in the aggregate but the per-skill `procedure_deviation: true` flag marks which two. Clean-only aggregate (excluding both rows): arm A 218650 / arm B 160056 / saved 58594 / pct_saved 27%. So the headline 13% saved is largely dragged down by the two compromised rows; without them, Opus saves 27% — much closer to Sonnet's 26%.

headline_finding: Across all 6 sampled skills, Opus saved 13% on average vs Sonnet's 26% on the same skills — the recipe-vs-cold gap roughly halved going from Sonnet to Opus. Three actionable patterns: (1) high-saving scaffolding skills compress less on Opus (review 63%→39%, copyright-scan 49%→16%), because Opus is more efficient cold; (2) clean pipeline-recipes hold their save rate (skill-localUpdate 52%→51%), because the recipe collapses pipeline-discovery work both models would otherwise repeat; (3) Opus narrows but doesn't always flip cost-more meta skills (readme-drift-sync -112%→-4%), because both arms get more thorough rather than just arm B. The absolute compute cost per skill goes UP on Opus regardless of save rate — audit doubled from 114K to 209K per arm. Implication for portfolio cost projections: if you run skills on Opus, multiply per-use cost by ~1.5-2× and shrink savings to 30-60% of the Sonnet-measured figure as a first pass.
caveats: N=1 per skill per arm. A second dispatch would land differently for both arms; the cross-arm direction (recipe saves vs costs) is more trustworthy than the absolute numbers.
Opus has access to the same tools as Sonnet sub-agents in this harness. If Opus had tool-access differences, the comparison would be confounded.

Stratified sample of 6 across 35 calibrated skills. Pattern claims (e.g., 'scaffolding skills save less on Opus') are projections from a small sample, not statistically validated across the full portfolio.
